title: Mackenzie spring volume and pulse width had no clear relation in 45 approved years from 1973 to 2019
abstract: We tested whether the positive Ob spring volume-width relation extends to the Mackenzie at Arctic Red River. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 and 45 complete approved years in 1973-2019. After linear year trends were removed, the correlation between log April-July volume and central 60% flow width was -0.063. Conditional 95% five-year block limits were -0.454 to 0.303. This is a separate basin and agency test within the same compilation. Fixed flow windows, shared flow errors, regulation, lake storage and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The test does not identify a physical cause, measure coastal delivery or establish forecast skill. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit support reproduction. Source and annual records remain external.

display.caption: Detrended spring volume and width at Mackenzie, and planned correlation checks. Bars give conditional 95% block limits. These are gauge metrics, not melt duration or coastal delivery.
